races.title: County Commissioner, District 6 (At-Large)
races.note: Countywide seat. County candidates may take at most $1,000 per donor per election. About 1 in 10 addresses in 34221 sit in County District 3, which has no district race this year — those voters see only this county commission race.

cands.name: Reggie Bellamy
cands.bio: Former District 2 county commissioner (2018-2022) and Port Authority chair (2021). Born in Bradenton; Army veteran (honorable discharge 1993, corporal); business-administration degree from Bethune-Cookman. Longtime Palmetto High basketball coach, middle-school dean and Executive Director of the Palmetto Youth Center. Lost 2022 re-election to Amanda Ballard after the district was redrawn.
cands.local_ties: Fifth-generation Manatee County resident per The Bradenton Times; Palmetto-based youth work. Home address not stated in the sources.

record.text: Won District 2 in 2018 by beating incumbent Charles Smith in the Democratic primary by 185 votes, then won the general election.
Elected Manatee County Port Authority chairman for one year (Dec 2020).

Late Oct / Nov 2020: voted against a motion to reconsider the county's $32.5M purchase of 161 acres (Musgrave family land beside the Lena Road landfill); the motion failed 4-3. The column links the push to reconsider to developer-backed interests (columnist's inference).
Supported redevelopment of the urban core (downtown Bradenton and Palmetto) and attainable housing (2022 candidate profile).

money_notes.text: Official SOE totals: $25,835 monetary through Oct 29, 2026, including $5,000 from himself; no political-committee gifts other than the county Democratic Executive Committee ($1,500). Largest outside givers: Scott and Barbara Brownell ($1,000 each), Gregory L. Patterson PA law firm ($1,000), Jeffrey Trinklein ($1,000). Almost no real-estate or development occupations in the filings (about $500).
In the 2022 Democratic primary Charles Smith claimed Bellamy took 'almost $100,000' from developers (Smith's claim; not verified).

controversies.text: 2018: then-Commissioner Charles Smith called for Bellamy to resign as Palmetto Youth Center executive director, saying 'He seldom shows up for work', and said he would not support future funding (the center received about $300,000-$400,000 a year from the children's services tax). Bellamy called the claims 'an unfortunate and false statement'. No finding or resignation was found.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: The Bradenton Times recommended Bellamy; the Manatee Democratic Executive Committee gave $1,500.

local_issue_stance.text: No stated position on the wetland buffer rollback or development found (he left the commission in Nov 2022, before the Oct 2023 rollback vote). His Oct 14, 2026 Bradenton Times podcast was not transcribed.

cands.name: Tara Poulton
cands.bio: District director / chief of staff to U.S. Rep. Vern Buchanan since 2023. Earlier: Manatee Chamber of Commerce VP (2021-23), Southwest Florida Water Management District government-affairs manager, Bradenton Area CVB, United Way of Manatee, DeSoto County government division director and spokesperson. MPA (FSU), BA (USF). Won a four-way GOP primary Aug 18, 2026 with 38.27%.
cands.local_ties: Lakewood Ranch (Greenbrook) resident; Manatee-based career since about 2013. The Observer article does not say how long she has lived there.

record.text: Chief of staff to Rep. Vern Buchanan's district office (Manatee and southern Hillsborough) since June 2023.
Hired by SWFWMD in 2013 as a government-affairs liaison for Sarasota, Manatee, Charlotte and DeSoto counties; the Observer says she worked on wetland issues there.
Served about three years as public information officer and division director in DeSoto County government (parks, library, social services, transit, economic development).
No votes cast as an elected official (first run for office).

money_notes.text: Official SOE totals: $82,051 monetary + $2,406 in-kind through Oct 29, 2026 (largest in the D6 field; Bellamy $25,835). In the itemized export: about $25,125 from business entities, about $10,000 from political committees (about 12%), about $46,900 from individuals.

Political committees that gave: Knowledge Is Power ($1,000), Gulf Coast Builders Exchange PC ($1,500), Realtors Political Advocacy / Activity / Action committees ($1,000 each), Keep Florida Moving Forward ($1,000), Focused on Florida's Future PC ($1,000), Christian Family Coalition-Manatee ($1,000), Firefighters and Paramedics PC ($1,000), Shumaker Florida Political Committee ($500).

Donors listing a real-estate, property or construction occupation or business type in the filing total about $14,700 (about 17.5% of receipts), e.g. OnPlace LLC, North Lake Communities Inc., McClure Holdings LLC, Orange Park LLC, VB Investments LLC. This is a keyword tally by the researcher, not a legal classification. Poulton told the Beacons she has accepted no money from developers.

The Bradenton Times (July) reports ten $1,000 maximum gifts from entities it links, via federal disclosures, to businesses owned by U.S. Rep. Vern Buchanan and family (e.g. Country Club Shores LLC, Auto Central Services Inc., Speedwing Investment Co., 1099 Management Co. LLC, MB Acquisitions & Leasing LLC, Aircraft One/Two LLC, Orange Park LLC, VB Investments LLC, VB Pointe West Investments LLC); Matt Buchanan also gave $1,000.

Also $1,000-$2,000 each from former Senate President Bill Galvano and his law firm Grimes Galvano, former House Speaker Richard Corcoran, Commissioners George Kruse and Tal Siddique, and farm/land interests (Bob Spencer / West Coast Tomato, Jones Potato Farm, McClure entities).

North Lake Communities Inc. ($1,000 to Poulton per SOE) is also listed by The Bradenton Times as a contributor to the Strong Communities of Southwest Florida PAC (lobbyist David Ramba), which funneled money to the Republican Party of Florida. The same article does not list Poulton as a recipient of that PAC network's money.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: Rep. Vern Buchanan and Bradenton Mayor Gene Brown (per Tampa Bay Beacons).

Commissioner George Kruse has encouraged her to run since 2022 (Observer). The Bradenton Times recommended her opponent and said Poulton drew heavy support from political operatives and PACs (editorial).

local_issue_stance.text: Says she supports maintaining wetland buffers and flood protection, wants to slow growth without stopping it and hold developers accountable.
Supports the Amendment 3 homestead measure (says the county would have to do more with less if it passes). Opposes expansion of Mosaic mining but would let current mining continue.

cands.name: Elizabeth "Liz" Arnold
cands.bio: Retired corporate treasury executive (about 23 years at Florida Power Corp./Duke Energy; 7 years City of St. Petersburg); long-time commission-meeting activist who worked alongside the late Commissioner Carol Felts. Won a six-way GOP primary Aug 18, 2026 with 27.96% for the seat left vacant by Felts's death in Feb 2026.
cands.local_ties: Moved from Pinellas to Myakka City around 1990; lives in Parrish on five acres and still owns 10 acres in Myakka (Observer). About 30 years in the county.

record.text: Roughly a decade of public comment at county and planning-commission meetings; says her involvement helped stop subdivisions and save a canopy road.

Helped Felts defend the Future Development Area Boundary; has spoken at meetings on stormwater fees, canopy roads, wetland protections, construction dust and phosphate mining (Observer; no specific wetland position stated).
No votes cast as an elected official (first run).

money_notes.text: Official SOE totals: $26,061 monetary + $2,658 in-kind. About $12,000 (about 46% of monetary receipts) is her own money. No political-committee contributions in the itemized export; largest outside gifts are $1,000 each (Mark Van De Ree, Yvonne Kelly, Fehl Safe Water Systems LLC, Quality Plumbing of Sarasota, individuals). A $500 'GrayRobinson PAC' entry is filed under the individual contribution type.

In the primary a network of PACs targeted her: Parents for Accountability in Education PAC (chair Terry Miller, a lobbyist whose registrations include Neal Communities) paid for texts; Just the Facts PAC received $159,500, nearly all from Miller's Southwest Florida Jobs Alliance, whose Manatee/Sarasota donors included Rye Associates LLC ($25,000; registered at Neal Communities' address; managers Michael Neal and Richard Bedford). Reported by The Bradenton Times, which endorsed Arnold.
Christian Family Coalition-Manatee PAC, funded by a $47,000 check from Christian Family Coalition Florida Inc., gave $1,000 to rival Mark Stanoch (per TBT); it is not shown giving to Arnold.

controversies.text: Primary-season PAC texts and signs said Arnold and her husband were under animal-welfare investigation and that he shot a dog. Record: a Feb 21, 2025 sheriff's report has Larry Arnold reporting he fired at a loose dog that attacked theirs; the deputy found no crime scene or injured dog. A county animal-services inquiry requested Aug 3, 2026 was closed Aug 13 without substantiating a violation. (Source is The Bradenton Times, which endorsed Arnold; MCSO said a printout showing the case 'active' was a clerical error.)

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: Your Observer recommended Mark Stanoch in the primary and did not recommend Arnold (called her earnest and civic-minded).

local_issue_stance.text: Says the county has too much development (about 65,000 homes in the pipeline) and suggests pausing new projects; opposes unsustainable growth; wants land-use agendas released earlier and an ombudsman.

cands.local_ties: Lifelong Palmetto resident per campaign profiles; his own 2022 survey lists a brother on the Palmetto city commission.

record.text: County commission 2014-2018: led the budget push for the long-promised North River pool in Palmetto (Bradenton Times, 2018).

controversies.text: During his first Palmetto commission term he was 'relieved from office' after pleading no contest to a felony charge involving bounced checks tied to his bail-bonds business (called an improper-banking matter in a sympathetic 2015 profile; year not given there).

cands.name: Amanda Ballard
cands.bio: Child-welfare attorney (nearly eight years, Children's Legal Services) elected in 2022 as the first Republican to hold District 2; 2026 First Vice Chair, Port Authority member, Tourist Development Council chair. J.D. University of South Carolina (2014), Florida Bar 2015. Won the Aug 18, 2026 GOP primary with 67.45%.
cands.local_ties: Moved to Manatee County after law school in 2014; lived in Oneco since 2015 (2022 profile). Her county bio names Manatee County, not a specific city.

record.text: Oct 5, 2023: voted with the majority to cut local wetland buffer protections back to state minimums (reported 5-1 with Kruse the lone no; the Observer's later account lists Ballard among six yes votes, so the tally differs between outlets). Buffers were restored in 2025 (Jan 7 motion 6-1; Apr 3, 2025 vote 5-1, Rahn no); the Observer did not state Ballard's vote on the restorations and reported she and Siddique urged deferring to the county attorney in Jan 2025.
Feb 18, 2026: voted yes on a 5-2 vote granting Mosaic a 14-year extension of its Four Corners mine master mining plan, calling it a 'difficult decision'.
Apr 20, 2023: moved a revote that removed Vanessa Baugh as chair and reinstated Kevin Van Ostenbridge (4-2), saying her earlier vote was 'not in the best interest of the county'.

2025: expressed concern that higher impact fees could drive businesses away (the article does not report her vote). At a July 2026 forum she acknowledged voting to move SeaPort Manatee oversight away from commissioners.
Spearheaded the Mixon Fruit Farms land purchase and opened Under One Roof, the county's first women's shelter (Observer's description).
Hired political consultant Anthony Pedicini (SimWins) in 2022; did not rehire him in 2024 (Observer).

money_notes.text: Official SOE totals: $105,031 monetary + $1,556 in-kind through Oct 29, 2026 (The Bradenton Times Oct 2 snapshot: $83,515). Itemized export: about $15,500 (14.4%) from 16 political committees; about $12,600 (11.7%) from donors listing affordable-housing, construction, land or real-estate occupations (keyword tally by the researcher).

Committees giving $1,000 each include Hillsborough United, Knowledge Is Power, Florida Courage, six Realtors committees, Christian Family Coalition, Keep Florida Moving Forward, Friends of Mike Rahn PAC, Firefighters and Paramedics, Government Reform & Integrity Task Force PAC (GRIT), Shumaker Florida Political Committee; GrayRobinson PAC $500.

GRIT PAC (established July 2026 by a David Ballard; Ballard's county bio names her husband as David, but no source says they are the same person) received $63,500, all from Tallahassee and Ramba-linked committees ($25,000 Committee for Justice, Transportation & Business; $10,500 each from Coalition for Better Care, Greater FL Leadership Group, Voters for Economic Growth) and gave her campaign $1,000.

Strong Communities of Southwest Florida PAC (lobbyist David Ramba) received $2.77M from Healthy Progress LLC; listed contributors include Pat Neal, NDC Construction, Benderson Development, Vengroff Investments, One Stop Housing, Blue Sky Communities, Waste Pro, Barrington Group, Rye Associates, North Lake Communities. Its money went to the Republican Party of Florida and, via other PACs, to GRIT and Friends of Mike Rahn PAC, which gave to Ballard.

Individual maximum donors include Richard Corcoran, Bill Galvano, Rep. Bill Conerly, Ryan Lieberman (Barrington Group; Suncoast Builders Association president), Mark Vengroff (One Stop Housing), Whiting Preston (farmer and developer behind SeaFlower), Janet Mixon, five Palmetto Canning-linked donors, and Commissioners Kruse, Rahn and Siddique. She says contributions come from friends, attorneys and two affordable-housing developers and do not control her votes.

controversies.text: Challenger Charles Smith accused her at a July 2026 forum of siding with Mosaic; she replied she had tried 50 child-protection cases.

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: The Bradenton Times recommended opponent Charles Smith.
Contributions from Realtors PACs, Firefighters and Paramedics PAC, Christian Family Coalition and Keep Florida Moving Forward (see money).

local_issue_stance.text: Voted for the 2023 wetland buffer rollback (see record); later publicly changed position, per the TBT editorial.
At the July 2026 forum: street homelessness deters customers; wants less reliance on construction and tourism; defended moving port control to professional management.

races.title: Manatee County Water Quality Protection, Overdevelopment Prevention, Natural Lands Preservation and Public Preserves General Obligation Bonds ($75M, 0.16 mill)

m.name: Manatee County Water Quality Protection, Overdevelopment Prevention, Natural Lands Preservation and Public Preserves General Obligation Bonds ($75M, 0.16 mill)
m.summary: Authorizes the county to levy an added 0.16 mill property tax and issue up to $75M in general obligation bonds (20-year maturity, annual audits) to buy, improve and maintain environmental lands and conservation easements (including farmland development rights) that protect drinking water and water quality. It sits on top of the 2020 measure (0.15 mill, $50M cap, passed with about 71%). A no vote ends the program per the county natural-resources director; land already protected stays protected.

who_funds_yes.text: Political committee 'Protect Water, Preserve Land': $45,050 monetary + $8,926 in-kind per the Supervisor of Elections; donors Florida Wildlife Corridor Foundation $22,500, Trust for Public Land about $15,800, NCDG Management LLC (Sarasota; business not named in the filing) $10,000, and individuals; spending went mainly to Simmer House (Fort Myers) for marketing.

who_funds_no.text: No organized opposition committee found; opposition is individual voters (e.g. Trent Wayman) citing cost of living and distrust of county handling of funds.

supporters.text: Commissioners Mike Rahn and Tal Siddique (Siddique expects Amendment 3 supporters to back it); Conservation Florida; Keep Manatee Beautiful; Big Water Trust; League of Women Voters of Manatee County (supports, demands oversight fixes).

fiscal.text: About $16 per $100,000 of taxable value per year (TBT); about $34 a year on the median homestead per county staff (WUSF); on a $300,000 home the Observer says the bill rises from $45 to $93, a $48 increase. Collections under the 2020 levy: $7.6M (2023), $8.9M (2024), over $10M (2025); a county committee document cites $2.9M a year for maintenance. A county Inspector General audit found commingling of millage and other funds ('confusion and lack of transparency'); the county committed to separate funds and reimburse out-of-scope spending (per the League of Women Voters).
